body.statement: Under assignment positivity, let \(N_j=(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0)\), \(w_j=(1,1,2,2)\), and \(\varepsilon_j=\sqrt{\log(2/\beta_j)/(2N_j)}\). Uniformly over compatible primitives with \(d\ge\kappa\), with probability at least \(1-\beta\), \[K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\subseteq[\inf K^{\star}-R,\sup K^{\star}+R]\cap[0,1],\qquad R=\frac{2}{\kappa}\sum_jw_j\varepsilon_j.\] In addition, \(\sup_P E_P[\{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-\operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}]=O(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}))\) for fixed marginal budgets. These claims use only the four marginal binomial laws and do not require their counts to be mutually independent.
body.justification: Coverage alone can be vacuous; the width theorem quantifies the statistical price of weak assay informativeness and four primitive intervals.
body.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 establishes uniform asymptotic coverage for generic moment projections but not an exact finite-sample width modulus indexed by the Youden floor.
body.consumer: Validation-study designers can translate a desired benefit-interval precision into trial and gold-standard stratum sizes.
